bookInfo.author: Sima Guang

sentences.zh: 資治通鑑 第206卷

translations.literal: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 206.
translations.idiomatic: Zizhi Tongjian, Volume 206.

sentences.zh: 卷第二百六

translations.literal: Volume 206.
translations.idiomatic: Volume 206.

sentences.zh: 【唐紀二十二】 起強圉作噩，盡上章困敦六月，凡三年有奇。

translations.literal: [Tang Annals 22] From Qiangyu Zuoe through the sixth month of Shangzhang Kundun; more than three years in all.
translations.idiomatic: [Tang Annals 22] From dingyou (697) through the sixth month of gengzi (700)—a little more than three years in all.

sentences.zh: 正月，己亥朔，太后享通天宮。

translations.literal: In the first month, on jihai, the first day of the new moon, the Empress Dowager offered sacrifice at the Tongtian Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month, on jihai, the new moon, the Empress Dowager offered sacrifice at the Tongtian Palace.

sentences.zh: 突厥默啜寇靈州，以許欽明自隨。

translations.literal: The Turk Mokuan raided Ling Prefecture, taking Xu Qinming with him.
translations.idiomatic: The Turk chieftain Mokuan invaded Ling Prefecture, taking Xu Qinming captive.

sentences.zh: 欽明至城下大呼，求美醬、粱米及墨，意欲城中選良將，引精兵、夜襲虜營，而城中無諭其意者。

translations.literal: When Qinming reached below the city walls he shouted loudly, requesting fine sauce, millet, and ink; his intent was for the city to choose a good general, lead picked troops, and raid the barbarian camp by night, but no one in the city understood his meaning.
translations.idiomatic: When Qinming reached the foot of the walls he cried out for fine sauce, millet, and ink—planning to have the city choose a capable general and lead elite troops in a night attack on the barbarian camp—but no one inside understood what he meant.

sentences.zh: 箕州刺史劉思禮學相人於術士張憬藏，憬藏謂思禮當歷箕州，位至太師。

translations.literal: Jizhou Inspector Liu Silu studied physiognomy under the adept Zhang Jingzang; Jingzang told Silu he would serve in Jizhou and rise to Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: Jizhou Inspector Liu Silu studied physiognomy under the adept Zhang Jingzang, who told him he would hold office in Jizhou and rise to Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 思禮念太師人臣極貴，非佐命無以致之，乃與洛州錄事參軍綦連耀謀反，陰結朝士，托相術，許人富貴，俟其意悅，因說以「綦連耀有天命，公必因之以得富貴。」

translations.literal: Silu reflected that Grand Preceptor was the utmost honor for a subject, unattainable except by aiding a founding ruler; he therefore plotted rebellion with Luozhou Registrar-Adjutant Qilian Yao, secretly winning court officials by means of physiognomy, promising men wealth and rank, and when they were pleased telling them, "Qilian Yao has the Mandate of Heaven; you will surely gain wealth and honor through him."
translations.idiomatic: Silu reasoned that Grand Preceptor was the highest rank a subject could hold, reachable only by aiding a founding sovereign; he plotted rebellion with Luozhou Registrar-Adjutant Qilian Yao, secretly recruiting court officials through fortune-telling, promising them wealth and rank, and when they were receptive telling them, "Qilian Yao has Heaven's mandate; you will surely rise through him."

sentences.zh: 鳳閣舍人王劇兼天官侍郎事，用思禮為箕州刺史。

translations.literal: Fengge Attendant Wang Ju, who also handled the duties of Vice Minister of the Bureau of Celestial Offices, appointed Silu inspector of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ju of Fengge, who was also acting Vice Minister of the Bureau of Celestial Offices, appointed Silu inspector of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 明堂尉河南吉頊聞其謀，以告合宮尉來俊臣，使上變告之。

translations.literal: Mingtang Commandant Ji Xu of Henan heard of the plot and told Hegong Commandant Lai Junchen, who had him submit an accusatory memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Mingtang Commandant Ji Xu of Henan learned of the plot and informed Hegong Commandant Lai Junchen, who had him lodge an accusatory memorial.

sentences.zh: 太后使河內王武懿宗推之。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager had Prince Wu Yizong of Henei investigate it.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager had Prince Wu Yizong of Henei investigate the case.

sentences.zh: 懿宗令思禮廣引朝士，許免其死，凡小忤意者皆引之。

translations.literal: Yizong had Silu implicate many court officials broadly, promising to spare their lives; all who had in any small way displeased him were implicated.
translations.idiomatic: Yizong had Silu implicate many court officials, promising to spare their lives; anyone who had even slightly offended him was named.

sentences.zh: 於是思禮引鳳閣侍郎同平章事李元素、夏官侍郎同平章事孫元亨、知天官侍郎事石抱忠、劉奇、給事中周譒及王勃兄涇州刺史勉、弟監察御史助等，凡三十六家，皆海內名士，窮楚毒以成其獄。

translations.literal: Thereupon Silu implicated Fengge Vice Minister and Associate Counselor Li Yuansu, Summer Offices Vice Minister and Associate Counselor Sun Yuanheng, Acting Vice Minister of Celestial Offices Shi Baozhong, Liu Qi, Supervising Censor Zhou Pu, and Wang Bo's elder brother Jingzhou Inspector Mian and younger brother Investigating Censor Zhu, thirty-six households in all, all famous men within the realm; extreme Chu torture was used to complete the cases.
translations.idiomatic: Silu then implicated Associate Counselors Li Yuansu and Sun Yuanheng, Acting Vice Minister of Celestial Offices Shi Baozhong, Liu Qi, Supervising Censor Zhou Pu, and Wang Bo's brothers Mian and Zhu—thirty-six households in all, every one a celebrated figure in the empire—subjecting them to the full rigor of Chu torture to force confessions.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，皆族誅之，親舊連坐流竄者千餘人。

translations.literal: On renxu, all were executed to the last of their clans; more than a thousand kin and associates were implicated and exiled.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu, all were executed along with their entire clans, and more than a thousand relatives and associates were banished as accomplices.

sentences.zh: 初，懿宗寬思禮於外，使誣引諸人。

translations.literal: Earlier, Yizong had kept Silu at ease outside custody so he could falsely implicate others.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Yizong had kept Silu at liberty outside the prison so he could falsely implicate others.

sentences.zh: 諸人既誅，然後收思禮，思禮悔之。

translations.literal: After the others had been executed, he then took Silu into custody; Silu regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: After the others had been executed, he finally arrested Silu, who was filled with remorse.

sentences.zh: 懿宗自天授以來，太后數使之鞫獄，喜誣陷人，時人以為周、來之亞。

translations.literal: Since the Tianshou era Yizong had often been sent by the Empress Dowager to interrogate cases; he delighted in framing people, and contemporaries regarded him as second only to Lai and Lai.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Tianshou era the Empress Dowager had repeatedly sent Yizong to interrogate prisoners; he delighted in framing the innocent, and contemporaries ranked him just below Zhou Xing and Lai Junchen.

sentences.zh: 來俊臣欲擅其功，復羅告吉頊；

translations.literal: Lai Junchen wished to monopolize the credit and again fabricated charges against Ji Xu;
translations.idiomatic: Lai Junchen, wanting sole credit for the case, fabricated charges against Ji Xu as well;

sentences.zh: 頊上變，得召見，僅免。

translations.literal: Xu submitted an accusatory memorial, was summoned to audience, and narrowly escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Xu lodged an accusatory memorial, was summoned to audience, and narrowly escaped punishment.

sentences.zh: 俊臣由是復用，而頊亦以此得進。

translations.literal: Junchen was thereby restored to favor, and Xu also advanced on this account.
translations.idiomatic: Junchen was thereby restored to favor, and Xu also advanced on the strength of this affair.

sentences.zh: 俊臣黨人羅告司刑府史樊惎謀反，誅之。

translations.literal: A partisan of Junchen fabricated charges that Bureau of Justice clerk Fan Ji plotted rebellion, and he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: One of Junchen's partisans fabricated charges that Bureau of Justice clerk Fan Ji was plotting rebellion, and Fan was executed.

sentences.zh: 惎子訟冤於朝堂，無敢理者，乃援刀自刳其腹。

translations.literal: Ji's son pleaded his father's innocence in the court hall; no one dared take up the case, so he seized a knife and disemboweled himself.
translations.idiomatic: Ji's son pleaded his father's innocence in the court hall; when no one dared hear the case, he seized a knife and cut open his own belly.

sentences.zh: 秋官侍郎上邽劉如璿見之，竊歎而泣。

translations.literal: Autumn Offices Vice Minister Liu Ruquan of Shanggui saw it and sighed and wept in secret.
translations.idiomatic: Autumn Offices Vice Minister Liu Ruquan of Shanggui saw it and wept in private dismay.

sentences.zh: 俊臣奏如璿黨惡逆，下獄，處以絞刑；

translations.literal: Junchen memorialized that Ruquan had sided with the wicked and rebellious; he was imprisoned and sentenced to strangulation;
translations.idiomatic: Junchen memorialized that Ruquan had abetted treason; he was imprisoned and sentenced to strangulation;

sentences.zh: 制流絞州。

translations.literal: an edict commuted this to exile in Jiaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: but an edict commuted the sentence to exile in Jiaozhou.

sentences.zh: 尚乘奉御張易之，行成之族孫也，年少，美姿容，善音律。

translations.literal: Palace Stud Groom Zhang Yizhi was a descendant of Zhang Xingcheng's clan; he was young, of handsome appearance, and skilled in music.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Stud Groom Zhang Yizhi, a descendant of Zhang Xingcheng's line, was young and handsome and skilled in music.

sentences.zh: 太平公主薦易之弟昌宗入侍禁中，昌宗復薦易之，兄弟皆得幸於太后，常傅朱粉，衣錦繡。

translations.literal: Princess Taiping recommended Yizhi's younger brother Changzong to attend within the inner palace; Changzong in turn recommended Yizhi; both brothers won the Empress Dowager's favor, constantly applying rouge and wearing brocade.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Taiping recommended Yizhi's younger brother Changzong for service in the inner palace; Changzong then recommended Yizhi in turn; both brothers won the Empress Dowager's favor, habitually rouging their faces and dressing in brocade.

sentences.zh: 昌宗累遷散騎常侍，易之為司衛少卿；

translations.literal: Changzong was repeatedly promoted to Regular Attendant of the Rapid Cavalry, and Yizhi became Vice Director of the Palace Guards;
translations.idiomatic: Changzong rose to Regular Attendant of the Rapid Cavalry, and Yizhi became Vice Director of the Palace Guards;

sentences.zh: 拜其母韋氏、臧氏為太夫人，賞賜不可勝紀，仍敕鳳閣侍郎李迥秀為臧氏私夫。

translations.literal: their mothers the Lady Wei and the Lady Zang were enfeoffed as Grand Ladies; rewards were beyond counting, and Fengge Vice Minister Li Huixiu was ordered to be Lady Zang's private consort.
translations.idiomatic: their mothers Lady Wei and Lady Zang were enfeoffed as Grand Ladies; rewards were beyond counting, and Fengge Vice Minister Li Huixiu was ordered to serve as Lady Zang's private consort.

sentences.zh: 迥秀，大亮之族孫也。

translations.literal: Huixiu was a descendant of Li Daliang's clan.
translations.idiomatic: Huixiu was a descendant of Li Daliang's line.

sentences.zh: 武承嗣、三思、懿宗、宗楚客、晉卿皆侯易之門庭，爭執鞭轡，謂易之為五郎，昌宗為六郎。

translations.literal: Wu Chengsi, Sansi, Yizong, Zong Chuke, and Jin Qing all waited at Yizhi's gate, vying to hold whip and bridle, calling Yizhi Fifth Lord and Changzong Sixth Lord.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Chengsi, Wu Sansi, Yizong, Zong Chuke, and Jin Qing all waited at Yizhi's gate, competing to hold his whip and bridle, calling Yizhi Fifth Lord and Changzong Sixth Lord.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，突厥默啜寇勝州，平狄軍副使安道買擊破之。

translations.literal: On guihai, the Turk Mokuan raided Sheng Prefecture; Pingdi Army Vice Commissioner An Daomai defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai, the Turk Mokuan invaded Sheng Prefecture; Pingdi Army Vice Commissioner An Daomai defeated him.

sentences.zh: 甲子，以原州司馬婁師德守鳳閣侍郎、同平章事。

translations.literal: On jiazi, Yuan Prefecture Administrator Lou Shide was made Acting Fengge Vice Minister and Associate Counselor.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi, Yuan Prefecture Administrator Lou Shide was appointed Acting Fengge Vice Minister and Associate Counselor.

sentences.zh: 春，三月，戊申，清邊道總管王孝傑、蘇宏暉等將兵十七萬與孫萬榮戰於東硤石谷，唐兵大敗，孝傑死之。

translations.literal: In spring, the third month, on wushen, Qingbian Circuit Commander Wang Xiaojie, Su Honghui, and others led one hundred seventy thousand troops to battle Sun Wanrong at East Xiashi Valley; Tang forces were greatly defeated and Xiaojie died.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the third month, on wushen, Qingbian Circuit Commander Wang Xiaojie and Su Honghui led one hundred seventy thousand troops against Sun Wanrong at East Xiashi Valley; the Tang army was routed and Xiaojie was killed.

sentences.zh: 孝傑遇契丹，帥精兵為前鋒，力戰。

translations.literal: Xiaojie encountered the Khitan, led picked troops as vanguard, and fought fiercely.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaojie met the Khitan, led elite troops as vanguard, and fought fiercely.

sentences.zh: 契丹引退，孝傑追之，行背懸崖，契丹回兵薄之，宏暉先遁，孝傑墜崖死，將士死亡殆盡。

translations.literal: The Khitan feigned retreat; Xiaojie pursued; marching with a cliff at their backs, the Khitan turned and pressed them; Honghui fled first; Xiaojie fell from the cliff and died; officers and soldiers were nearly all killed.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan feigned retreat; Xiaojie pursued them along a cliffside road; the Khitan wheeled about and closed in; Honghui fled first; Xiaojie fell from the cliff and died; officers and soldiers were nearly wiped out.

sentences.zh: 管記洛陽張說馳奏其事。

translations.literal: Luoyang Recorder Zhang Yue urgently memorialized the affair.
translations.idiomatic: Luoyang Recorder Zhang Yue sent an urgent memorial reporting the disaster.

sentences.zh: 太后贈孝傑官爵，遣使斬宏暉以徇；

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager posthumously enfeoffed Xiaojie with rank and title and sent an envoy to behead Honghui as a public example;
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager posthumously enfeoffed Xiaojie and sent an envoy to execute Honghui as a public warning;

sentences.zh: 使者未至，宏暉以立功得免。

translations.literal: before the envoy arrived, Honghui was spared because he had rendered merit in battle.
translations.idiomatic: but before the envoy arrived, Honghui was spared on account of merit earned in battle.

sentences.zh: 武攸宜軍漁陽，聞孝傑等敗沒，軍中震恐，不敢進。

translations.literal: Wu Youyi's army was at Yuyang; hearing that Xiaojie and the others had been destroyed, the army was shaken with fear and dared not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Youyi's army was at Yuyang; when word came that Xiaojie and his force had been destroyed, the troops were shaken with fear and dared not advance.

sentences.zh: 契丹乘勝寇幽州，攻陷城邑，剽掠吏民，攸宜遣將擊之，不克。

translations.literal: The Khitan pressed their victory to raid You Prefecture, captured cities and towns, and plundered officials and people; Youyi sent generals to strike them but could not overcome them.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan pressed their victory, raided You Prefecture, captured towns, and plundered officials and commoners; Youyi sent generals against them but could not prevail.

sentences.zh: 閻知微、田歸道同使突厥，冊默啜為可汗。

translations.literal: Yan Zhiwei and Tian Guidao were joint envoys to the Turks to invest Mokuan as qaghan.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Zhiwei and Tian Guidao served jointly as envoys to the Turks to invest Mokuan as qaghan.

sentences.zh: 知微中道遇默啜使者，輒與之緋袍、銀帶，且上言：「虜使至都，宜大為供張。」

translations.literal: Zhiwei met Mokuan's envoys on the road and at once gave them scarlet robes and silver belts, and memorialized: "When the barbarian envoys reach the capital, they should be entertained on a grand scale."
translations.idiomatic: Zhiwei met Mokuan's envoys en route and at once gave them scarlet robes and silver belts, memorializing, "When the barbarian envoys reach the capital, they should be entertained on a grand scale."

sentences.zh: 歸道上言：「突厥背誕積年，方今悔過，宜待聖恩寬宥。

translations.literal: Guidao memorialized: "The Turks have rebelled for many years; now that they repent, they should await the sage grace of pardon.
translations.idiomatic: Guidao memorialized, "The Turks have rebelled for many years; now that they repent, they should await imperial clemency.

sentences.zh: 今知微擅與之袍帶，使朝廷無以復加；

translations.literal: Now Zhiwei has on his own authority given them robes and belts, leaving the court nothing further to bestow;
translations.idiomatic: Zhiwei has on his own authority given them robes and belts, leaving the court nothing further to bestow;

sentences.zh: 宜令反初服以俟朝恩。

translations.literal: they should be made to return to their original dress and await the court's grace.
translations.idiomatic: they should be made to return to their original dress and await the court's grace.

sentences.zh: 又，小虜使臣，不足大為供張。」

translations.literal: Moreover, these are minor barbarian envoys and do not warrant grand entertainment."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, these are minor barbarian envoys and do not warrant grand entertainment."

sentences.zh: 太后然之。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager approved.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager agreed.

sentences.zh: 知微見默啜，舞蹈，吮其靴鼻；

translations.literal: When Zhiwei met Mokuan he danced and licked the toe of his boot;
translations.idiomatic: When Zhiwei met Mokuan he danced and kissed the toe of his boot;

sentences.zh: 歸道長揖不拜。

translations.literal: Guidao made a long bow but did not prostrate himself.
translations.idiomatic: Guidao made a long bow but refused to prostrate himself.

sentences.zh: 默啜囚歸道，將殺之，歸道辭色不撓，責其無厭，為陳禍福。

translations.literal: Mokuan imprisoned Guidao and was about to kill him; Guidao's words and bearing did not waver; he reproached Mokuan's insatiability and set forth fortune and misfortune for him.
translations.idiomatic: Mokuan imprisoned Guidao and was about to kill him; Guidao's words and bearing never faltered; he reproached Mokuan's greed and laid out the consequences of fortune and ruin.

sentences.zh: 阿波達干元珍曰：「大國使者，不可殺也。」

translations.literal: Apo Dagan Yuanzhen said, "An envoy of a great state must not be killed."
translations.idiomatic: Apo Dagan Yuanzhen said, "An envoy of a great power must not be killed."

sentences.zh: 默啜怒稍解，但拘留不遣。

translations.literal: Mokuan's anger eased somewhat, but he detained Guidao and would not release him.
translations.idiomatic: Mokuan's anger eased somewhat, but he detained Guidao and would not let him go.

sentences.zh: 初，鹹亨中，突厥有降者，皆處之豐、勝、靈、夏、朔、代六州，至是，默啜求六州降戶及單于都護府之地，並谷種、繒帛、農器、鐵，太后不許。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the Xianheng era, Turks who surrendered were all settled in the six prefectures of Feng, Sheng, Ling, Xia, Shuo, and Dai; at this time Mokuan requested the surrendered households of the six prefectures and the territory of the Chanyu Protectorate, together with grain seed, silks, farm tools, and iron; the Empress Dowager did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in the Xianheng era, surrendering Turks had been settled in the six prefectures of Feng, Sheng, Ling, Xia, Shuo, and Dai; now Mokuan demanded those surrendered households, the territory of the Chanyu Protectorate, grain seed, silks, farm tools, and iron; the Empress Dowager refused.

sentences.zh: 默啜怒，言辭悖慢。

translations.literal: Mokuan was angry and his words were insolent and disrespectful.
translations.idiomatic: Mokuan grew angry and his words turned insolent and disrespectful.

sentences.zh: 姚□、楊再思以契丹未平，請依默啜所求給之。

translations.literal: Yao [□] and Yang Zaisi, because the Khitan had not yet been pacified, asked that Mokuan's requests be granted.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Yuanchong and Yang Zaisi, because the Khitan rebellion was not yet suppressed, urged that Mokuan's demands be met.

sentences.zh: 麟台少監、知鳳閣侍郎贊皇李嶠曰：「戎狄貪而無信，此所謂『借寇兵資盜糧』也，不如治兵以備之。」

translations.literal: Lintai Vice Director and Acting Fengge Vice Minister Li Qiao of Zanhuang said, "The barbarians are greedy and faithless; this is what is called 'lending weapons to the bandit and provisions to the thief'; it would be better to train troops and prepare against them."
translations.idiomatic: Lintai Vice Director and Acting Fengge Vice Minister Li Qiao of Zanhuang said, "The barbarians are greedy and untrustworthy; this is lending arms to the enemy and grain to a thief. We would do better to train troops and prepare our defenses."

sentences.zh: □、再思固請與之，乃悉驅六州降戶數千帳以與默啜，並給谷種四萬斛，雜彩五萬段，農器三千事，鐵數萬斤，並許其昏。

translations.literal: [□] and Zaisi firmly pressed to give these things; thereupon several thousand households of surrendered people from the six prefectures were all driven out and given to Mokuan, together with forty thousand hu of grain seed, fifty thousand lengths of mixed silks, three thousand sets of farm tools, tens of thousands of jin of iron, and permission for a marriage alliance.
translations.idiomatic: Yao and Zaisi pressed their case, and several thousand surrendered households from the six prefectures were driven out to Mokuan, together with forty thousand hu of grain seed, fifty thousand lengths of mixed silks, three thousand sets of farm tools, tens of thousands of jin of iron, and permission for a marriage alliance.

sentences.zh: 默啜由是益強。

translations.literal: Mokuan thereby grew still stronger.
translations.idiomatic: Mokuan thereby grew still stronger.

sentences.zh: 田歸道始得還，與閻知微爭論於太后前。

translations.literal: When Tian Guidao at last returned, he and Yan Zhiwei argued before the Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: When Tian Guidao at last returned, he and Yan Zhiwei argued their cases before the Empress Dowager.

sentences.zh: 歸道以為默啜必負約，不可恃和親，宜為之備。

translations.literal: Guidao held that Mokuan would surely break the agreement and that one could not rely on marriage alliance; preparations should be made.
translations.idiomatic: Guidao argued that Mokuan would surely break his word and that marriage alliance was no security; defenses should be prepared.

sentences.zh: 知微以為和親必可保。

translations.literal: Zhiwei held that marriage alliance would surely guarantee peace.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiwei insisted that marriage alliance would surely guarantee peace.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，鑄九鼎成，徙置通天宮。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, the casting of the Nine Cauldrons was completed and they were moved to the Tongtian Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, the Nine Cauldrons were cast and moved to the Tongtian Palace.

sentences.zh: 豫州鼎高丈八尺，受千八百石；

translations.literal: The Yuzhou cauldron was one zhang eight chi high and held one thousand eight hundred shi;
translations.idiomatic: The Yuzhou cauldron stood one zhang eight chi high and held one thousand eight hundred shi;

sentences.zh: 餘州高丈四尺，受千二百石；

translations.literal: the others were one zhang four chi high and held one thousand two hundred shi;
translations.idiomatic: the others stood one zhang four chi high and held one thousand two hundred shi;

sentences.zh: 各圖山川物產於其上，共用銅五十六萬七百餘斤。

translations.literal: on each were depicted mountains, rivers, and local products; five hundred sixty thousand seven hundred-odd jin of bronze were used in all.
translations.idiomatic: each was decorated with its province's mountains, rivers, and products; more than five hundred sixty thousand jin of bronze were used in all.

sentences.zh: 太后欲以黃金千兩塗之，姚□曰：「九鼎神器，貴於天質自然。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager wished to gild them with one thousand liang of gold; Yao [□] said, "The Nine Cauldrons are sacred vessels; their value lies in the natural quality Heaven gave them.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager wished to gild them with one thousand liang of gold; Yao Yuanchong said, "The Nine Cauldrons are sacred vessels; their worth lies in the natural quality Heaven gave them.

sentences.zh: 且臣觀其五采煥炳相雜，不待金色以為炫耀。」

translations.literal: Moreover, I observe that their five colors blaze and mingle; they need no gold for display."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, their five colors already blaze and mingle; they need no gold for display."

sentences.zh: 太后從之。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager accepted his counsel.

sentences.zh: 自玄武門曳入，令宰相、諸王帥南北牙宿衛兵十餘萬人並仗內大牛、白象共曳之。

translations.literal: They were dragged in through the Xuanwu Gate; the Empress Dowager ordered the chief ministers and princes to lead more than one hundred thousand guards of the northern and southern yamen, together with great oxen and white elephants from within the palace precincts, to drag them together.
translations.idiomatic: They were dragged in through the Xuanwu Gate; the chief ministers and princes led more than one hundred thousand guards of the northern and southern yamen, together with great oxen and white elephants from the palace precincts, to haul them in.

sentences.zh: 前益州長史王及善已致仕，會契丹作亂，山東不安，起為滑州刺史。

translations.literal: Former Yizhou Chief Administrator Wang Jishan had already retired; when the Khitan rebelled and Shandong was unsettled, he was recalled to serve as prefect of Hua.
translations.idiomatic: Former Yizhou Chief Administrator Wang Jishan had retired; when the Khitan rebelled and Shandong grew unsettled, he was recalled as prefect of Hua.

sentences.zh: 太后召見，問以朝廷得失，及善陳治亂之要十餘條。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager summoned him to audience and asked about the court's strengths and failings; Jishan set forth more than ten essentials of order and disorder.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager summoned him and asked about the court's strengths and failings; Jishan laid out more than ten essentials of good and bad government.

sentences.zh: 太后曰：「外州末事，此為根本，卿不可出。」

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager said, "An outer prefecture is a minor matter; this is the root—my lord must not leave."
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager said, "A provincial post is a minor matter; this capital is the root—you must not leave."

sentences.zh: 癸酉，留為內史。

translations.literal: On guiyou he was retained as Inner Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou he was retained as Inner Secretary.

sentences.zh: 癸未，以右金吾衛大將軍武懿宗為神兵道行軍大總管，與右豹韜衛將軍何迦密將兵擊契丹。

translations.literal: On guiwei, Right Golden Canopy Guard General Wu Yizong was made Grand Commander of the Shenbing Circuit campaign army, and with Right Leopard Bow Guard General He Jiami led troops to strike the Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei, Right Golden Canopy Guard General Wu Yizong was made Grand Commander of the Shenbing campaign army and, with Right Leopard Bow Guard General He Jiami, led troops against the Khitan.

sentences.zh: 五月，癸卯，又以婁師德為清邊道副大總管，右武威衛將軍沙吒忠義為前軍總管，將兵二十萬擊契丹。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on guimao, Lou Shide was also made Deputy Grand Commander of the Qingbian Circuit, Right Martial Might Guard General Shazha Zhongyi was made Vanguard Commander, and they led two hundred thousand troops to strike the Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on guimao, Lou Shide was also made Deputy Grand Commander of the Qingbian Circuit, Right Martial Might Guard General Shazha Zhongyi was made Vanguard Commander, and they led two hundred thousand troops against the Khitan.

sentences.zh: 先是，有朱前疑者，上書云：「臣夢陛下壽滿八百。」

translations.literal: Earlier there was one Zhu Qianyi, who memorialized, "Your servant dreamed that Your Majesty's lifespan would reach eight hundred."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier there was a man named Zhu Qianyi who memorialized, "Your servant dreamed that Your Majesty would live eight hundred years."

sentences.zh: 即拜拾遺。

translations.literal: He was at once appointed Remonstrator.
translations.idiomatic: He was at once appointed Remonstrator.

sentences.zh: 又自言「夢陛下發白再玄，齒落更生。」

translations.literal: He also said of himself, "I dreamed that Your Majesty's white hair turned black again and fallen teeth grew anew."
translations.idiomatic: He also claimed, "I dreamed that Your Majesty's white hair turned black again and fallen teeth grew back."

sentences.zh: 遷駕部郎中。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Director in the Imperial Transport Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Director in the Imperial Transport Bureau.

sentences.zh: 出使還，上書云：「聞嵩山呼萬歲。」

translations.literal: Returning from a mission abroad, he memorialized, "I heard Mount Song cry 'Ten thousand years!'"
translations.idiomatic: Returning from a mission abroad, he memorialized, "I heard Mount Song cry 'Long live the sovereign!'"

sentences.zh: 賜以緋算袋，時未五品，於綠衫上佩之。

translations.literal: He was granted a scarlet tally-pouch; as he had not yet reached the fifth rank, he wore it on his green robe.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted a scarlet tally-pouch; though he had not yet reached the fifth rank, he wore it on his green robe.

sentences.zh: 會發兵討契丹，敕京官出馬一匹供軍，酬以五品。

translations.literal: When troops were raised to campaign against the Khitan, capital officials were ordered to furnish one horse each for the army, rewarded with fifth-rank status.
translations.idiomatic: When troops were raised against the Khitan, capital officials were ordered to furnish one horse each for the army, with fifth-rank status as reward.

sentences.zh: 前疑買馬輸之，屢抗表求進階；

translations.literal: Qianyi bought a horse and presented it, repeatedly submitting memorials demanding advancement;
translations.idiomatic: Qianyi bought a horse and presented it, repeatedly demanding promotion;

sentences.zh: 太后惡其貪鄙，六月，乙丑，敕還其馬，斥歸田裡。

translations.literal: the Empress Dowager detested his greed and baseness; in the sixth month, on yichou, an edict returned his horse and dismissed him to his fields.
translations.idiomatic: the Empress Dowager detested his greed; in the sixth month, on yichou, an edict returned his horse and sent him back to his fields.

sentences.zh: 右司郎中馮翊喬知之有美妾曰碧玉，知之為之不昏。

translations.literal: Right Department Director Qiao Zhizhi of Fengyi had a beautiful concubine named Biyu; because of her Zhizhi did not marry.
translations.idiomatic: Right Department Director Qiao Zhizhi of Fengyi had a beautiful concubine named Biyu; for her sake he never married.

sentences.zh: 武承嗣藉以教諸姬，遂留不還。

translations.literal: Wu Chengsi borrowed her to instruct his concubines and then kept her and would not return her.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Chengsi borrowed her to instruct his concubines and then kept her and would not return her.

sentences.zh: 知之作《綠珠怨》詩以寄之，碧玉赴井死。

translations.literal: Zhizhi composed the poem "Lament for Green Pearl" and sent it to her; Biyu threw herself into a well and died.
translations.idiomatic: Zhizhi wrote the poem "Lament for Green Pearl" and sent it to her; Biyu threw herself into a well and died.

sentences.zh: 承嗣得詩於裙帶，大怒，諷酷吏羅告，族之。

translations.literal: Chengshi found the poem in her sash, was greatly angered, and prompted harsh officials to fabricate charges; Zhizhi's clan was executed to the last.
translations.idiomatic: Chengshi found the poem in her sash, flew into a rage, and had harsh officials fabricate charges; Zhizhi's entire clan was executed.

sentences.zh: 司僕少卿來俊臣倚勢貪淫，士民妻妾有美者，百方取之；

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Palace Stud Lai Junchen relied on power and was greedy and lecherous; when officials or commoners had beautiful wives or concubines, he took them by every means;
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director of the Palace Stud Lai Junchen abused his power with greed and lust; whenever an official or commoner had a beautiful wife or concubine, he seized her by every means;

sentences.zh: 或使人羅告其罪，矯稱敕以取其妻，前後羅織誅人，不可勝計。

translations.literal: or he had men fabricate charges, falsely citing an edict to seize the wife; before and after, those he framed and executed were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: or he had men fabricate charges and falsely cite an edict to seize the wife; the men he framed and executed were beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 自宰相以下，籍其姓名而取之。

translations.literal: From the chief ministers downward he registered their names and took them.
translations.idiomatic: From the chief ministers downward he kept a register of names and took what he wanted.

sentences.zh: 自言才比石勒。

translations.literal: He said of himself that his talent matched Shi Le's.
translations.idiomatic: He boasted that his talent matched that of Shi Le.

sentences.zh: 監察御史李昭德素惡俊臣，又嘗庭辱秋官侍郎皇甫文備，二人共誣昭德謀反，下獄。

translations.literal: Investigating Censor Li Zhaode had long hated Junchen and had once publicly humiliated Autumn Offices Vice Minister Huangfu Wenbei; the two jointly framed Zhaode for plotting rebellion, and he was imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: Investigating Censor Li Zhaode had long hated Junchen and had once publicly humiliated Autumn Offices Vice Minister Huangfu Wenbei; the two jointly framed Zhaode for treason and had him imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 俊臣欲羅告武氏諸王及太平公主，又欲誣皇嗣及廬陵王與南北牙同反，冀因此盜國權，河東人衛遂忠告之。

translations.literal: Junchen wished to fabricate charges against the princes of the Wu clan and Princess Taiping, and also wished to frame the Crown Prince and the Prince of Luling together with the northern and southern yamen guards in one rebellion, hoping thereby to seize state power; Wei Sui of Hedong warned them in confidence.
translations.idiomatic: Junchen planned to frame the Wu princes and Princess Taiping, and also to implicate the Crown Prince and the Prince of Luling together with the northern and southern yamen guards in a single treason plot, hoping thereby to seize state power; Wei Sui of Hedong warned them in secret.

sentences.zh: 諸武及太平公主恐懼，共發其罪，繫獄，有司處以極刑。

translations.literal: The Wu princes and Princess Taiping were afraid; they jointly exposed his crimes; he was imprisoned and the authorities sentenced him to the extreme penalty.
translations.idiomatic: The Wu princes and Princess Taiping were terrified; they jointly exposed his crimes; he was imprisoned and the authorities sentenced him to death.

sentences.zh: 太后欲赦之，奏上三日，不出。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager wished to pardon him; the memorial lay before her three days without issue.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager wished to pardon him; the memorial lay before her three days without a decision.

sentences.zh: 王及善曰：「俊臣凶狡貪暴，國之元惡，不去之，必動搖朝廷。」

translations.literal: Wang Jishan said, "Junchen is fierce, cunning, greedy, and violent—the state's chief villain; if he is not removed, the court will surely be shaken."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jishan said, "Junchen is fierce, cunning, greedy, and violent—the state's chief villain; if he is not removed, the court itself will be shaken."

sentences.zh: 太后游苑中，吉頊執轡，太后問以外事，對曰：「外人唯怪來俊臣奏不下。」

translations.literal: While the Empress Dowager was touring the park, Ji Xu held the reins; she asked him about outside affairs, and he replied, "Those outside only wonder why the memorial on Lai Junchen has not been issued."
translations.idiomatic: While the Empress Dowager was touring the park, Ji Xu held the reins; she asked about affairs outside, and he replied, "People outside only wonder why the memorial on Lai Junchen has not been decided."

sentences.zh: 太后曰：「俊臣有功於國，朕方思之。」

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager said, "Junchen has rendered merit to the state; We are still considering it."
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager said, "Junchen has served the state; I am still considering the matter."

sentences.zh: 頊曰：「於安遠告虺貞反，既而果反，今止為成州司馬。

translations.literal: Xu said, "When Yu Anyuan reported Huaizhen's rebellion, Huaizhen did indeed rebel afterwards—yet now he holds nothing more than the post of Chengzhou Administrator.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Xu said, "Yu Anyuan reported Prince Huaizhen's rebellion, and Huaizhen did rebel as he said—yet now Yu holds nothing more than the post of Chengzhou Administrator.

sentences.zh: 俊臣聚結不逞，誣構良善，贓賄如山，冤魂塞路，國之賊也，何足惜哉！」

translations.literal: Junchen gathers the lawless, frames the good, bribes pile like mountains, wronged souls choke the roads—he is the state's traitor; what is there to regret!"
translations.idiomatic: Junchen gathers criminals, frames the innocent, amasses bribes beyond counting, and fills the roads with the wrongfully dead—he is a traitor to the state. Why spare him!"

sentences.zh: 太后乃下其奏。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager then issued his memorial.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager then approved his memorial.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，昭德、俊臣同棄市，時人無不痛昭德而快俊臣。

translations.literal: On dingmao, Zhaode and Junchen were both executed in the marketplace; people of the time all grieved for Zhaode and rejoiced at Junchen.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao, Zhaode and Junchen were both executed in the marketplace; contemporaries mourned Zhaode and rejoiced at Junchen's fate.

sentences.zh: 仇家爭啖俊臣之肉，斯須而盡，抉眼剝面，披腹出心，騰蹋成泥。

translations.literal: Enemies vied to eat Junchen's flesh; in an instant it was gone—they gouged out his eyes, flayed his face, split his belly and removed his heart, trampling him into mud.
translations.idiomatic: His enemies fought over Junchen's flesh until it was gone in moments; they gouged out his eyes, flayed his face, split open his belly and tore out his heart, trampling what remained into mud.

sentences.zh: 太后知天下惡之，乃下制數其罪惡，且曰：「宜加赤族之誅，以雪蒼生之憤，可准法籍沒其家。」

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager knew all under heaven hated him and issued an edict enumerating his crimes, saying, "The extermination of his entire clan should be added to wipe away the common people's wrath; his household may be confiscated according to law."
translations.idiomatic: Knowing how universally he was hated, the Empress Dowager issued an edict listing his crimes and declaring, "His entire clan should be exterminated to satisfy the people's wrath, and his property confiscated by law."

sentences.zh: 士民皆相賀於路曰：「自今眠者背始帖席矣！」

translations.literal: Officials and commoners all congratulated each other on the road, saying, "From now on those who sleep can at last lay their backs flat on the mat!"
translations.idiomatic: Officials and commoners congratulated one another in the streets, saying, "From now on we can sleep with our backs flat on the mat!"

sentences.zh: 俊臣以告綦連耀功，賞奴婢十人。

translations.literal: Junchen was rewarded with ten female servants for reporting Qilian Yao's rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: For reporting Qilian Yao's rebellion, Junchen was rewarded with ten female servants.

sentences.zh: 俊臣閱司農婢，無可者，以西突厥可汗斛瑟羅家有細婢，善歌舞，欲得以為賞口，乃使人誣告斛瑟羅反。

translations.literal: Junchen inspected female servants of the Ministry of Revenue and found none suitable; hearing that Western Turkic Khaghan Ashina Qieluo had a slender maid skilled in song and dance, he wished to obtain her as a reward servant and so had men falsely accuse Qieluo of rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Junchen inspected the Ministry of Revenue's female servants and found none to his liking; learning that Western Turkic Khaghan Ashina Qieluo had a slender maid skilled in song and dance, he wanted her as a reward and had men falsely accuse Qieluo of rebellion.

sentences.zh: 諸酋長詣闕割耳剺面訟冤者數十人。

translations.literal: Several dozen tribal chiefs came to court, cutting off their ears and slashing their faces to plead their innocence.
translations.idiomatic: Several dozen tribal chiefs came to court, mutilating their ears and faces to protest their innocence.

sentences.zh: 會俊臣誅，乃得免。

translations.literal: When Junchen was executed, they were spared.
translations.idiomatic: When Junchen was executed, they were finally cleared.

sentences.zh: 俊臣方用事，選司受其屬請不次除官者，每銓數百人。

translations.literal: While Junchen was in power, the Selection Bureau, receiving his clients' requests for out-of-turn appointments, each session processed several hundred.
translations.idiomatic: While Junchen held power, the Selection Bureau processed hundreds of out-of-turn appointments at each session on his clients' requests.

sentences.zh: 俊臣敗，侍郎皆自首。

translations.literal: After Junchen's fall, the vice ministers all confessed.
translations.idiomatic: After Junchen fell, the vice ministers all confessed their misconduct.

sentences.zh: 太后責之，對曰：「臣負陛下，死罪！

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager reproached them; they replied, "Your servant has failed Your Majesty—a capital offense!
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager rebuked them; they replied, "We have failed Your Majesty—a capital offense!

sentences.zh: 臣亂國家法，罪止一身；

translations.literal: Your servant violated the state's laws; the crime stops with one person alone;
translations.idiomatic: We violated state law, and that crime rests on us alone;

sentences.zh: 違俊臣語，立見滅族。」

translations.literal: disobey Junchen's word, and one's clan is immediately exterminated."
translations.idiomatic: but disobey Junchen's orders and one's entire clan would be wiped out at once."

sentences.zh: 太后乃赦之。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager then pardoned them.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager then pardoned them.

sentences.zh: 上林令侯敏素諂事俊臣，其妻董氏諫之曰：「俊臣國賊，指日將敗，君宜遠之。」

translations.literal: Superintendent of the Upper Park Hou Min had long fawned on Junchen; his wife Lady Dong admonished him, saying, "Junchen is a traitor to the state and will fall any day—you should keep your distance."
translations.idiomatic: Superintendent of the Upper Park Hou Min had long fawned on Junchen; his wife Lady Dong warned him, "Junchen is a traitor to the state and will fall any day. You should keep your distance."

sentences.zh: 敏從之。

translations.literal: Min followed her advice.
translations.idiomatic: Min took her advice.

sentences.zh: 俊臣怒，出為武龍令。

translations.literal: Junchen was angered and had him sent out as magistrate of Wulong.
translations.idiomatic: Junchen was furious and had him posted as magistrate of Wulong.

sentences.zh: 敏欲不住，妻曰：「速去勿留！」

translations.literal: Min wished not to go; his wife said, "Go quickly—do not stay!"
translations.idiomatic: Min hesitated to leave; his wife said, "Go at once—do not linger!"

sentences.zh: 俊臣敗，其黨皆流嶺南，敏獨得免。

translations.literal: When Junchen fell, his faction were all exiled to Lingnan; Min alone was spared.
translations.idiomatic: When Junchen fell, his followers were all exiled to Lingnan; Min alone escaped punishment.

sentences.zh: 太后征於安遠為尚食奉御，擢吉頊為右肅政中丞。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager summoned Yu Anyuan as Food Service Attendant and promoted Ji Xu to Right Censor-in-Chief of the Righteous Governance Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager recalled Yu Anyuan as Food Service Attendant and promoted Ji Xu to Right Censor-in-Chief of the Righteous Governance Bureau.

sentences.zh: 以檢校夏官侍郎宗楚客同平章事。

translations.literal: Acting Summer Offices Vice Minister Zong Chuke was made Associate Counselor.
translations.idiomatic: Acting Summer Offices Vice Minister Zong Chuke was appointed Associate Counselor.

sentences.zh: 武懿宗軍至趙州，聞契丹將駱務整數千騎將至冀州，懿宗懼，欲南遁。

translations.literal: Wu Yizong's army reached Zhao Prefecture; hearing that Khitan general Luo Wuzheng was leading several thousand horsemen toward Ji Prefecture, Yizong was afraid and wished to flee south.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Yizong's army reached Zhao Prefecture; when he heard that the Khitan general Luo Wuzheng was advancing with several thousand horsemen toward Ji Prefecture, Yizong panicked and wanted to flee south.

sentences.zh: 或曰：「虜無輜重，以抄掠為資，若按兵拒守，勢必離散，從而擊之，可有大功。」

translations.literal: Someone said, "The barbarians have no baggage train and live by raiding; if we hold our position and defend, they will necessarily scatter—strike them then and great merit can be won."
translations.idiomatic: Someone advised, "The enemy has no supply train and lives by raiding. Hold your ground and they will scatter—then strike, and you can win a great victory."

sentences.zh: 懿宗不從，退據相州，委棄軍資器仗甚眾。

translations.literal: Yizong did not follow; he withdrew to Xiang Prefecture, abandoning vast military stores and weapons.
translations.idiomatic: Yizong refused; he withdrew to Xiang Prefecture, abandoning enormous quantities of military supplies and weapons.

sentences.zh: 契丹遂屠趙州。

translations.literal: The Khitan then massacred Zhao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan then sacked and massacred Zhao Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 甲午，孫萬榮為奴所殺。

translations.literal: On jiawu, Sun Wanrong was killed by his slave.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu, Sun Wanrong was killed by his own slave.

sentences.zh: 萬榮之破王孝傑也，於柳城西北四百里依險築城，留其老弱婦女、所獲器仗資財，使妹夫乙冤羽守之，引精兵寇幽州。

translations.literal: When Wanrong defeated Wang Xiaojie, four hundred li northwest of Liucheng he built a fort relying on difficult terrain, leaving the old, weak, and women, captured weapons, and wealth, with his brother-in-law Yi Yuanyu to guard it, and led picked troops to raid You Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After defeating Wang Xiaojie, Wanrong built a fortified camp four hundred li northwest of Liucheng, leaving the elderly, women, captured weapons, and plunder in the care of his brother-in-law Yi Yuanyu while he led elite troops to raid You Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 恐突厥默啜襲其後，遣五人至黑沙，語默啜曰：「我已破王孝傑百萬之人，唐人破膽，請與可汗乘勝共取幽州。」

translations.literal: Fearing the Turk Mokuan would strike from the rear, he sent five men to Heisha, saying to Mokuan, "I have already broken Wang Xiaojie's force of a million; the Tang have lost their nerve—please join the khaghan in riding the victory to take You Prefecture together."
translations.idiomatic: Fearing a rear attack from the Turks, he sent five envoys to Heisha to tell Mokuan, "I have already shattered Wang Xiaojie's army of a million men; the Tang are terrified. Join me in pressing the advantage to seize You Prefecture."

sentences.zh: 三人先至，默啜喜，賜以緋袍。

translations.literal: Three arrived first; Mokuan was pleased and rewarded them with crimson robes.
translations.idiomatic: Three arrived first; Mokuan was delighted and rewarded them with crimson robes.

sentences.zh: 二人後至，默啜怒其稽緩，將殺之，二人曰：「請一言而死。」

translations.literal: Two arrived later; Mokuan was angry at their delay and was about to kill them; the two said, "Grant us one word before we die."
translations.idiomatic: Two arrived later; Mokuan, angry at their delay, was about to execute them when they said, "Allow us one word before we die."

sentences.zh: 默啜問其故，二人以契丹之情告。

translations.literal: Mokuan asked the reason; the two told him the Khitan's true situation.
translations.idiomatic: Mokuan asked why; the two men revealed the Khitan's true situation.

sentences.zh: 默啜乃殺前三人而賜二人緋，使為鄉導，發兵取契丹新城，殺所獲涼州都督許欽明以祭天；

translations.literal: Mokuan then killed the first three and rewarded the two with crimson robes, making them guides; he sent troops to take the Khitan's New City, killing the captured Liangzhou Protector-General Xu Qinming to sacrifice to Heaven;
translations.idiomatic: Mokuan then executed the first three envoys, rewarded the two with crimson robes, and used them as guides; he marched on the Khitan's New City and sacrificed the captured Liangzhou Protector-General Xu Qinming to Heaven;

sentences.zh: 圍新城三日，克之，盡俘以歸。

translations.literal: he besieged New City for three days, took it, and brought all captives back.
translations.idiomatic: after a three-day siege he captured the city and took all its people captive.

sentences.zh: 使乙冤羽馳報萬榮。

translations.literal: He had Yi Yuanyu ride swiftly to report to Wanrong.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Yi Yuanyu racing back to inform Wanrong.

sentences.zh: 時萬榮方與唐兵相持，軍中聞之，恟懼。

translations.literal: At the time Wanrong was locked in stalemate with Tang troops; the army heard this and panicked.
translations.idiomatic: Wanrong was then locked in stalemate with Tang forces; when his army heard the news, it fell into panic.

sentences.zh: 奚人叛萬榮，神兵道總管楊玄基擊其前，奚兵擊其後，獲其將何阿小。

translations.literal: Xi people rebelled against Wanrong; Shenbing Circuit Commander Yang Xuanji struck from the front and Xi troops from the rear, capturing his general He Axiao.
translations.idiomatic: The Xi turned against Wanrong; Shenbing Circuit Commander Yang Xuanji attacked from the front while Xi forces struck from the rear, capturing his general He Axiao.

sentences.zh: 萬榮軍大潰，帥輕騎數千東走。

translations.literal: Wanrong's army collapsed in great rout; he led several thousand light cavalry east in flight.
translations.idiomatic: Wanrong's army collapsed; he fled east with several thousand light cavalry.

sentences.zh: 前軍總管張九節遣兵邀之於道，萬榮窮蹙，與其奴逃至潞水東，息於林下，歎曰：「今欲歸唐，罪已大。

translations.literal: Forward Army Commander Zhang Jiujie sent troops to intercept him on the road; Wanrong, hard pressed, fled with his slave east of the Lu River, rested under the trees, and sighed, "If I wish to return to Tang now, my guilt is already great.
translations.idiomatic: Forward Army Commander Zhang Jiujie sent troops to cut him off; hard pressed, Wanrong fled with his slave to the east bank of the Lu River and rested under the trees, sighing, "If I return to Tang now, my crimes are too great.

sentences.zh: 歸突厥亦死，歸新羅亦死。

translations.literal: Return to the Turks and I die; return to Silla and I die.
translations.idiomatic: Return to the Turks and I die; return to Silla and I die.

sentences.zh: 將安之乎！」

translations.literal: Where then am I to go!"
translations.idiomatic: Where can I go!"

sentences.zh: 奴斬其首以降，梟之四方館門。

translations.literal: His slave cut off his head and surrendered; it was displayed at the gate of the Hostel for Tributary Envoys.
translations.idiomatic: His slave cut off his head and surrendered; the head was displayed at the gate of the Hostel for Tributary Envoys.

sentences.zh: 其餘眾及奚、□皆降於突厥。

translations.literal: The remaining troops and the Xi and [□] all surrendered to the Turks.
translations.idiomatic: The remaining troops, together with the Xi and other tribes, all surrendered to the Turks.

sentences.zh: 戊子，特進武承嗣、春官尚書武三思並同鳳閣鸞台三品。

translations.literal: On wuzi, specially advanced Wu Chengsi and Spring Offices Minister Wu Sansi were both made Counselors of Third Rank at Fengge and Luantai.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi, Wu Chengsi, specially advanced, and Spring Offices Minister Wu Sansi were both appointed Counselors of Third Rank at Fengge and Luantai.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，制以契丹初平，命河內王武懿宗、婁師德及魏州刺史狄仁傑分道安撫河北。

translations.literal: On xinmao, an edict, since the Khitan had just been pacified, ordered Prince of Henei Wu Yizong, Lou Shide, and Wei Prefecture Inspector Di Renjie to pacify Hebei by separate routes.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao, an edict declared that with the Khitan rebellion newly suppressed, Prince of Henei Wu Yizong, Lou Shide, and Wei Prefecture Inspector Di Renjie were to pacify Hebei by separate routes.

sentences.zh: 懿宗所至殘酷，民有為契丹所脅從復來歸者，懿宗皆以為反，生刳取其膽。

translations.literal: Where Yizong went he was cruel; commoners who had been coerced to follow the Khitan and came back, Yizong all treated as rebels and live-gutted to remove their gall.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever Yizong went he was brutal; commoners who had been forced to follow the Khitan and then returned home were all treated as rebels, live-gutted, and their gall extracted.

sentences.zh: 先是，何阿小嗜殺人，河北人為之語曰：「唯此兩何，殺人最多。」

translations.literal: Earlier, He Axiao loved killing people; people of Hebei made a saying: "Of these two He alone, none kill more."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, He Axiao was bloodthirsty; people in Hebei had a saying: "These two He—no one kills more than they do."

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，丁酉，昆明內附，置竇州。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on dingyou, Kunming submitted, and Dou Prefecture was established.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on dingyou, the Kunming people submitted, and Dou Prefecture was established.

sentences.zh: 武承嗣、武三思並罷政事。

translations.literal: Wu Chengsi and Wu Sansi were both removed from government affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Chengsi and Wu Sansi were both removed from office.

sentences.zh: 庚午，武攸宜自幽州凱旋。

translations.literal: On gengwu, Wu Youyi returned in triumph from You Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu, Wu Youyi returned in triumph from You Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 武懿宗奏河北百姓從賊者請盡族之，左拾遺王求禮庭折之曰：「此屬素無武備，力不勝賊，苟從之以求生，豈有叛國之心！

translations.literal: Wu Yizong memorialized that Hebei commoners who followed the bandits should have their clans exterminated; Left Reminder Wang Qiuli rebutted him in court, saying, "These people have never had military preparations and lacked strength to overcome the bandits; if they followed to preserve their lives, how could they have had hearts to rebel against the state!
translations.idiomatic: Wu Yizong memorialized that all Hebei commoners who had followed the rebels should have their clans exterminated; Left Reminder Wang Qiuli rebutted him in open court, saying, "These people had no means of defense and could not resist the enemy; they followed only to survive. How could they have meant to betray the state!

sentences.zh: 懿宗擁強兵數十萬，望風退走，賊徒滋蔓，又欲移罪於草野詿誤之人，為臣不忠，請先斬懿宗以謝河北！」

translations.literal: Yizong commanded several hundred thousand strong troops, yet fled at the first sight of the enemy; the bandits spread unchecked, and now he wishes to shift blame onto rustics who were misled—this is disloyal service; I beg you first behead Yizong to appease Hebei!"
translations.idiomatic: Yizong commanded an army of several hundred thousand yet fled at the first sign of the enemy, letting the rebels spread unchecked—and now he wants to shift the blame onto innocent rustics! That is disloyal service. I beg you execute Yizong first to appease Hebei!"

sentences.zh: 懿宗不能對。

translations.literal: Yizong could not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Yizong had no answer.

sentences.zh: 司刑卿杜景儉亦奏：「此皆脅從之人，請悉原之。」

translations.literal: Minister of Punishments Du Jingjian also memorialized, "These are all people coerced to follow; I ask that all be pardoned."
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Punishments Du Jingjian also memorialized, "These are all people who were coerced into following the rebels. I ask that all be pardoned."

sentences.zh: 太后從之。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager agreed.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager agreed.

sentences.zh: 八月，丙戌，納言姚□坐事左遷益州長史，以太子宮尹豆盧欽望為文昌右相、鳳閣鸞台三品。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on bingxu, Counselor of State Yao [□] was demoted for an offense to chief administrator of Yizhou; Palace Superintendent of the Crown Prince Doulu Qinwang was made Left Vice Director of the Literary Flourishing Bureau and Counselor of Third Rank at Fengge and Luantai.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on bingxu, Counselor of State Yao Yuanchong was demoted for an offense to chief administrator of Yizhou; Palace Superintendent of the Crown Prince Doulu Qinwang was appointed Left Vice Director of the Literary Flourishing Bureau and Counselor of Third Rank at Fengge and Luantai.

sentences.zh: 九月，壬辰，大享通天宮，赦天下，改元。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on renchen, a great sacrifice was offered at the Tongtian Palace; the realm was pardoned and the era name was changed.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on renchen, the court offered a great sacrifice at the Tongtian Palace, proclaimed a general amnesty, and changed the era name.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，婁師德守納言。

translations.literal: On gengxu, Lou Shide was made acting Counselor of State.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu, Lou Shide was appointed acting Counselor of State.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，太后謂侍臣曰：「頃者周興、來俊臣按獄，多連引朝臣，雲其謀反；

translations.literal: On jiayin, the Empress Dowager said to her attendants, "Recently Zhou Xing and Lai Junchen investigated cases and implicated many court officials, saying they plotted rebellion;
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin, the Empress Dowager said to her attendants, "Recently Zhou Xing and Lai Junchen investigated cases and implicated many court officials on charges of treason;

sentences.zh: 國有常法，朕安敢違！

translations.literal: the state has fixed laws—how would We dare violate them!
translations.idiomatic: the state has fixed laws—how could I dare violate them!

sentences.zh: 中間疑其不實，使近臣就獄引問，得其手狀，皆自承服，朕不以為疑。

translations.literal: In between We suspected it was untrue and sent close ministers to the prison to lead questioning; obtaining their written confessions, all personally acknowledged guilt—We were not suspicious.
translations.idiomatic: When I doubted the truth of the charges, I sent close ministers to the prisons to question the accused; they obtained written confessions, and all acknowledged guilt—I had no reason to doubt.

sentences.zh: 自興、俊臣死，不復聞有反者，然則前死者不有冤邪？」

translations.literal: Since Xing and Junchen died, We no longer hear of rebels—then were not those who died before wrongly accused?"
translations.idiomatic: Since Xing and Junchen died, I have heard of no further rebels—then were not those executed before wrongly accused?"

sentences.zh: 夏官侍郎姚元崇對曰：「自垂拱以來坐謀反死者，率皆興等羅織，自以為功。

translations.literal: Summer Offices Vice Minister Yao Yuanchong replied, "Since the Chuigong era those executed for plotting rebellion have mostly all been framed by Xing and the rest, who made it their merit.
translations.idiomatic: Summer Offices Vice Minister Yao Yuanchong replied, "Since the Chuigong era, nearly everyone executed for treason was framed by Xing and his ilk, who counted it as merit.

sentences.zh: 陛下使近臣問之，近臣亦不自保，何敢動搖！

translations.literal: Your Majesty sent close ministers to question them, but close ministers could not even protect themselves—how would they dare to waver!
translations.idiomatic: When Your Majesty sent close ministers to question the prisoners, those ministers could not even protect themselves—how would they dare challenge the confessions!

sentences.zh: 所問者若有翻覆，懼遭慘毒，不若速死。

translations.literal: Those questioned, if they changed their testimony, feared cruel torture—it was better to die quickly.
translations.idiomatic: If the accused recanted, they feared cruel torture; a quick death was preferable.

sentences.zh: 賴天啟聖心，興等伏誅，臣以百口為陛下保，自今內外之臣無復反者；

translations.literal: Thanks to Heaven opening the sage heart, Xing and the rest were executed; your servant pledges the lives of a hundred mouths that from now on no official within or without will rebel again;
translations.idiomatic: Heaven opened Your Majesty's eyes, and Xing and his accomplices were executed; I pledge the lives of my entire household that from now on no official, within or without the court, will plot rebellion again;

sentences.zh: 若微有實狀，臣請受知而不告之罪。」

translations.literal: if there is even the slightest truth to it, your servant asks to receive the crime of knowing and not reporting."
translations.idiomatic: and if there is even the slightest truth to such charges, I ask to be punished for knowing and failing to report."

sentences.zh: 太后悅曰：「向時宰相皆順成其事，陷朕為淫刑之主；

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager was pleased and said, "Formerly the chief ministers all went along to complete these matters, trapping Us as a ruler of excessive punishments;
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager was pleased and said, "Formerly the chief ministers all went along with these prosecutions, making me a ruler of cruel punishments;

sentences.zh: 聞卿所言，深合朕心。」

translations.literal: hearing what you say deeply accords with Our heart."
translations.idiomatic: what you say accords deeply with my own mind."

sentences.zh: 賜元崇錢千緡。

translations.literal: She rewarded Yuanchong with one thousand strings of cash.
translations.idiomatic: She rewarded Yuanchong with one thousand strings of cash.

sentences.zh: 時人多為魏元忠訟冤者，太后復召為肅政中丞。

translations.literal: Many at the time pleaded Wei Yuanzhong's innocence; the Empress Dowager recalled him as Censor-in-Chief of the Righteous Governance Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Many people at the time pleaded Wei Yuanzhong's innocence; the Empress Dowager recalled him as Censor-in-Chief of the Righteous Governance Bureau.

sentences.zh: 元忠前後坐棄市流竄者四。

translations.literal: Yuanzhong had four times faced execution in the marketplace or exile.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhong had four times faced execution or exile.

sentences.zh: 嘗侍宴，太后問曰：「卿往者數負謗，何也？」

translations.literal: Once at a banquet the Empress Dowager asked, "You have several times borne slander—why?"
translations.idiomatic: Once at a banquet the Empress Dowager asked, "You have been slandered so many times—why?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「臣猶鹿耳，羅織之徒欲得臣肉為羹，臣安所避之！」

translations.literal: He replied, "Your servant is like a deer—the framers wish to have my flesh for broth; where could I avoid it!"
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "I am like a deer—the framers want my flesh for broth. Where could I hide!"

sentences.zh: 冬，閏十月，甲寅，以幽州都督狄仁傑為鸞台侍郎，司刑卿杜景儉為鳳閣侍郎，並同平章事。

translations.literal: In winter, the intercalary tenth month, on jiayin, You Prefecture Governor Di Renjie was made Luantai Vice Minister and Minister of Punishments Du Jingjian was made Fengge Vice Minister, both Associate Counselors.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the intercalary tenth month, on jiayin, You Prefecture Governor Di Renjie was appointed Luantai Vice Minister and Minister of Punishments Du Jingjian was appointed Fengge Vice Minister, both as Associate Counselors.

sentences.zh: 仁傑上疏，以為：「天生四夷，皆在先王封略之外，故東拒滄海，西阻流沙，北橫大漠，南阻五嶺，此天所以限夷狄而隔中外也。

translations.literal: Renjie submitted a memorial, holding that: "Heaven gave birth to the four barbarians, all outside the former kings' boundaries; thus the east is blocked by the blue sea, the west by shifting sands, the north by the great desert, and the south by the Five Ridges—this is how Heaven limits the barbarians and separates inner and outer.
translations.idiomatic: Renjie submitted a memorial arguing that: "Heaven created the four barbarian quarters all beyond the domains of the ancient kings: the east bounded by the sea, the west by shifting sands, the north by the great desert, and the south by the Five Ridges—this is how Heaven set the barbarians apart from the civilized world.

sentences.zh: 自典籍所紀，聲教所及，三代不能至者，國家盡兼之矣。

translations.literal: From what the canonical records note and civilization reaches, what the Three Dynasties could not attain, the state has all encompassed.
translations.idiomatic: By every measure recorded in the classics and every reach of civilization, territories the Three Dynasties never controlled have all been brought under the state's sway.

sentences.zh: 詩人矜薄伐於太原，美化行於江、漢，則三代之遠裔，皆國家之域中也。

translations.literal: The poet praised the modest campaign at Taiyuan, and civilization extended to the Yangtze and Han—then the distant descendants of the Three Dynasties were all within the state's domain.
translations.idiomatic: When the poets praised the modest campaign at Taiyuan and civilization reached the Yangtze and Han, even the remotest lands known to the Three Dynasties lay within the state's domain.

sentences.zh: 若乃用武荒外，邀功絕域，竭府庫之實以爭不毛之地，得其人不足增賦，獲其土不可耕織，苟求冠帶遠夷之稱，不務固本安人之術，此秦皇、漢武之所行，非五帝、三王之事業也。

translations.literal: If one uses force in the wild outer lands, seeks merit in the farthest regions, exhausts the treasury's substance to contest barren ground—gaining its people is insufficient to increase taxes, obtaining its soil cannot be tilled or woven—merely seeking the title of cap-and-sash distant barbarians, not devoting oneself to the art of strengthening the root and settling the people—this is what the First Emperor of Qin and Han Wudi did, not the enterprise of the Five Emperors and Three Kings.
translations.idiomatic: But to use force in distant wastelands, seek glory at the ends of the earth, and drain the treasury to seize barren ground—where the people add nothing to the tax rolls and the soil cannot be farmed or woven—is merely to win the empty praise of distant barbarians in caps and sashes, not to strengthen the foundation and settle the people. That is the way of the First Emperor of Qin and Emperor Wu of Han, not the enterprise of the sage kings.

sentences.zh: 始皇窮兵極武，務求廣地，死者如麻，至天下潰叛。

translations.literal: The First Emperor exhausted troops and extreme force, striving to expand territory; the dead piled like hemp until the realm collapsed in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: The First Emperor exhausted his armies in endless campaigns to expand his territory; the dead piled up like hemp until the realm collapsed in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 漢武征伐四夷，百姓困窮，盜賊蜂起；

translations.literal: Han Wudi campaigned against the four barbarians; the common people were destitute and bandits swarmed;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu campaigned against the four quarters; the people were driven to destitution and bandits swarmed;

sentences.zh: 末年悔悟，息兵罷役，故能為天所祐。

translations.literal: in his later years he repented, ceased troops and halted corvée, and so was able to be protected by Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: only in his later years, when he repented and halted the wars, was he able to regain Heaven's favor.

sentences.zh: 近者國家頻歲出師，所費滋廣，西戍西鎮，東戍安東，調發日加，百姓虛弊。

translations.literal: Recently the state has sent troops year after year; expenses grow ever wider—garrisoning the Western Regions in the west and Andong in the east, levies and deployments increase daily, and the common people are drained and exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years the state has sent armies out year after year at ever greater cost—garrisoning the Western Regions in the west and Andong in the east—while levies mount daily and the people are exhausted.

sentences.zh: 今關東饑饉，蜀、漢逃亡，江、淮已南，徵求不息，人不復業，相率為盜，本根一搖，憂患不淺。

translations.literal: Now east of the Pass there is famine; in Shu and Han people flee; south of the Yangtze and Huai, exactions never cease; people no longer return to their occupations and join together as bandits—once the root is shaken, the troubles are not shallow.
translations.idiomatic: Now famine grips the east, people flee from Shu and Han, and south of the Yangtze and Huai exactions never cease; people abandon their livelihoods and turn to banditry. Once the foundation is shaken, the troubles will be grave.

sentences.zh: 其所以然者，皆以爭蠻貊不毛之地，乖子養蒼生之道也。

translations.literal: The reason for this is entirely that we contest barren barbarian lands, departing from the way of nourishing the common people as children.
translations.idiomatic: The reason is that we are fighting over barren barbarian wastelands, contrary to the duty of nourishing the people.

sentences.zh: 昔漢元納賈捐之之謀而罷朱崖郡，宣帝用魏相之策而棄車師之田，豈不欲慕尚虛名，蓋憚勞人力也。

translations.literal: Formerly Han Yuan accepted Jia Juanzhi's plan and abolished Zhuya Commandery; Emperor Xuan used Wei Xiang's strategy and abandoned the fields of Jushi—was it that they did not wish to pursue empty fame? They feared exhausting human labor.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Emperor Yuan accepted Jia Juanzhi's advice and abolished Zhuya Commandery, and Emperor Xuan followed Wei Xiang's counsel and abandoned the Gaochang territories—not because they scorned glory, but because they feared wasting human labor.

sentences.zh: 近貞觀年中克平九姓，立李思摩為可汗，使統諸部者，蓋以夷狄叛則伐之，降則撫之，得推亡固存之義，無遠戍勞人之役，此近日之令典，經邊之故事也。

translations.literal: Recently in the Zhenguan era the Nine Surnames were conquered and Li Simo was established as khaghan to command the tribes—this was because when barbarians rebel, strike them; when they submit, soothe them, obtaining the principle of supporting the failing and preserving the enduring, without distant garrison corvée to weary the people—this is the recent fine model and the established precedent of border governance.
translations.idiomatic: In the recent Zhenguan era, when the Nine Tribes were subdued, Li Simo was installed as khaghan to rule the tribes—because when barbarians rebel, strike them, and when they submit, soothe them. That upheld the principle of supporting the failing and preserving the enduring without distant garrisons that weary the people. This is the recent model and the established precedent for border governance.

sentences.zh: 竊謂宜立阿史那斛瑟羅為可汗，委之四鎮，繼高氏絕國，使守安東。

translations.literal: Your servant privately holds that Ashina Qieluo should be established as khaghan, entrusted with the Four Garrisons, succeeding the Gao clan's extinct state to guard Andong.
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully propose that Ashina Qieluo be installed as khaghan, entrusted with the Four Garrisons, and set to guard Andong in succession to the extinct Gao kingdom.

sentences.zh: 省軍費於遠方，並甲兵於塞上，使夷狄無侵侮之患則可矣，何必窮其窟穴，與螻蟻校長短哉！

translations.literal: Save military expenses in distant places, concentrate armor and troops on the frontier, and ensure the barbarians have no calamity of invasion and insult—that is enough; why must we exhaust their lairs and measure lengths with ants!
translations.idiomatic: Save military expenses abroad, concentrate forces on the frontier, and ensure the barbarians pose no threat of invasion—that is enough. Why exhaust ourselves rooting out their lairs and contesting every inch of ground with them!

sentences.zh: 但當敕邊兵，謹守備，遠斥侯，聚資糧，待其自致，然後擊之。

translations.literal: One need only command frontier troops to guard preparations carefully, post distant scouts, gather provisions, wait for the enemy to come of themselves, and then strike.
translations.idiomatic: Simply order the frontier troops to maintain strict defenses, post distant scouts, stock provisions, wait for the enemy to come to us, and then strike.

sentences.zh: 以逸待勞則戰士力倍，以主御客則我得其便，堅壁清野則寇無所得；

translations.literal: Awaiting the weary with ease doubles the warriors' strength; as host facing guest we gain advantage; fortifying walls and clearing the countryside leaves the bandits with nothing to gain;
translations.idiomatic: Awaiting the weary with rested troops doubles our strength; fighting on our own ground gives us the advantage; fortifying walls and clearing the countryside leaves the enemy with nothing to seize;

sentences.zh: 自然賊深入則有顛躓之慮，淺入必無虜獲之益。

translations.literal: naturally if bandits penetrate deeply they will have fear of stumbling; if they penetrate shallowly they will surely gain no benefit of captives and booty.
translations.idiomatic: if they penetrate deeply they will fear being cut off; if they raid shallowly they will gain no worthwhile booty.

sentences.zh: 如此數年，可使二虜不擊而服矣。」

translations.literal: Thus for several years, the two barbarians can be made to submit without striking."
translations.idiomatic: In a few years the two barbarian powers can be made to submit without a fight."

sentences.zh: 事雖不行，識者是之。

translations.literal: Though the proposal was not adopted, those who understood approved it.
translations.idiomatic: Though the proposal was not adopted, those who understood the issue approved it.

sentences.zh: 鳳閣舍人李嶠知天官選事，始置員外官數千人。

translations.literal: Fengge Drafting Official Li Qiao oversaw Celestial Offices selections and for the first time established several thousand supernumerary officials.
translations.idiomatic: Fengge Drafting Official Li Qiao oversaw Celestial Offices selections and for the first time created several thousand supernumerary officials.

sentences.zh: 先是歷官以是月為正月，以臘月為閏。

translations.literal: Earlier, calendar officials had taken this month as the first month and the twelfth month as intercalary.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, the calendar officials had designated this month as the first month and the twelfth month as the intercalary month.

sentences.zh: 太后欲正月甲子朔冬至，乃下制以為：「去晦仍見月，有爽天經。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager wished the first day of the first month, jiazi, on the new moon, to coincide with the winter solstice, and issued an edict stating: "On the last day of the month the moon is still visible—this conflicts with the heavenly principle.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager wanted the new moon on jiazi, the first day of the first month, to fall on the winter solstice, and issued an edict declaring, "When the last day of the month still shows the moon, that violates the heavenly norm.

sentences.zh: 可以今月為閏月，來月為正月。」

translations.literal: This month may serve as an intercalary month, and the coming month may be the first month."
translations.idiomatic: Let this month be made intercalary, and the coming month be the first month."

sentences.zh: 正月，甲子朔，冬至，太后享通天宮；

translations.literal: In the first month, on jiazi, the new moon, the day of the winter solstice, the Empress Dowager offered sacrifice at the Tongtian Palace;
translations.idiomatic: In the first month, on jiazi, the new moon and the winter solstice, the Empress Dowager sacrificed at the Tongtian Palace;

sentences.zh: 赦天下，改元。

translations.literal: She granted amnesty to all under Heaven and changed the reign era.
translations.idiomatic: She proclaimed a general amnesty and changed the reign title.

sentences.zh: 夏官侍郎宗楚客罷政事。

translations.literal: Summer Offices Vice Minister Zong Chuke was removed from participation in state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Summer Offices Vice Minister Zong Chuke was dismissed from the conduct of government.

sentences.zh: 春，二月，乙未，文昌右相、同鳳閣鸞台三品豆盧欽望罷為太子賓客。

translations.literal: In spring, the second month, on yiwei, Wenchang Right Chancellor and Associate Third-Rank Counselor of Tongfengge and Luantai Dou Lu Qinwang was removed and made Grand Mentor to the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the second month, on yiwei, Wenchang Right Chancellor and Associate Third-Rank Counselor of Tongfengge and Luantai Dou Lu Qinwang was removed from office and appointed Grand Mentor to the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 武承嗣、三思營求為太子，數使人說太后曰：「自古天子未有以異姓為嗣者。」

translations.literal: Wu Chengsi and Wu Sansi schemed to become crown prince and repeatedly sent men to tell the Empress Dowager, saying, "From antiquity no Son of Heaven has ever made someone of a different surname his heir."
translations.idiomatic: Wu Chengsi and Wu Sansi maneuvered to become crown prince and repeatedly sent men to tell the Empress Dowager, "Since antiquity no emperor has ever named someone of another surname as his successor."

sentences.zh: 太后意未決。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager's mind was not yet decided.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager had not yet made up her mind.

sentences.zh: 狄仁傑每從容言於太后曰：「文皇帝櫛風沐雨，親冒鋒鏑，以定天下，傳之子孫。

translations.literal: Di Renjie would each time calmly speak to the Empress Dowager, saying, "Emperor Wen endured wind and rain and bathed in the storm, personally faced sword and arrow, to settle all under Heaven and pass it to his descendants.
translations.idiomatic: Di Renjie would calmly say to the Empress Dowager, "Emperor Wen braved wind and rain, faced sword and arrow in person, settled the realm, and passed it to his descendants.

sentences.zh: 太帝以二子托陛下。

translations.literal: The Great Emperor entrusted his two sons to Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong entrusted his two sons to Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 陛下今乃欲移之他族，無乃非天意乎！

translations.literal: Your Majesty now wishes to transfer the succession to another clan—might this not go against Heaven's will!
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty now wishes to shift the succession to another house—is that not against Heaven's intent!

sentences.zh: 且姑侄之與母子孰親？

translations.literal: Moreover, between aunt-and-nephew and mother-and-son, which bond is closer?
translations.idiomatic: And between aunt and nephew, and mother and son—which tie is closer?

sentences.zh: 陛下立子，則千秋萬歲後，配食太廟，承繼無窮；

translations.literal: If Your Majesty installs a son, then after a thousand autumns and ten thousand years you will receive offerings in the Grand Ancestral Temple and the succession will continue without end;
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty establishes a son as heir, then after a thousand years you will share offerings in the Grand Ancestral Temple and the line will continue without end;

sentences.zh: 立侄，則未聞侄為天子而祔姑於廟者也。」

translations.literal: If you install a nephew, one has never heard of a nephew as Son of Heaven enshrining his aunt in the temple."
translations.idiomatic: If you establish a nephew, one never hears of a nephew who becomes emperor enshrining his aunt in the ancestral temple."

sentences.zh: 太后曰：「此朕家事，卿勿預知。」

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager said, "This is my family's business—do not presume to know in advance."
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager said, "This is my family's affair. Do not meddle."

sentences.zh: 仁傑曰：「王者為四海為家，四海之內，孰非臣妾，何者不為陛下家事！

translations.literal: Renjie said, "The king takes all under Heaven as his household; within the Four Seas, who is not your subject—what is not the Empress Dowager's family business!
translations.idiomatic: Renjie said, "The ruler takes all within the Four Seas as his home. Who under Heaven is not your subject? What affair is not Your Majesty's family business!

sentences.zh: 君為元首，臣為股肱，義同一體，況臣備位宰相，豈得不預知乎！」

translations.literal: The ruler is the head and ministers the arms and legs—in principle one body; moreover, as I hold the post of chancellor, how could I not be informed!"
translations.idiomatic: The ruler is the head and ministers the arms and legs—we are one body in principle. And as I hold the chancellorship, how can I not be told!"

sentences.zh: 又勸太后召還廬陵王。

translations.literal: He also urged the Empress Dowager to recall the Prince of Luling.
translations.idiomatic: He also urged the Empress Dowager to recall the Prince of Luling.

sentences.zh: 王方慶、王及善亦勸之。

translations.literal: Wang Fangqing and Wang Jishan also urged this.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Fangqing and Wang Jishan urged the same.

sentences.zh: 太后意稍寤。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager's mind was slightly awakened.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager's mind began to turn.

sentences.zh: 他日，又謂仁傑曰：「朕夢大鸚鵡兩翅皆折，何也？」

translations.literal: Another day she again said to Renjie, "I dreamed of a great parrot with both wings broken—what does it mean?"
translations.idiomatic: Another day she said to Renjie, "I dreamed of a great parrot with both wings broken. What does it mean?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「武者，陛下之姓，兩翼，二子也。

translations.literal: He replied, "Wu is Your Majesty's surname; the two wings are your two sons.
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Wu is Your Majesty's surname. The two wings are your two sons.

sentences.zh: 陛下起二子，則兩翼振矣。」

translations.literal: If Your Majesty raises up your two sons, both wings will stir again."
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty restores your two sons, both wings will spread again."

sentences.zh: 太后由是無立承嗣、三思之意。

translations.literal: From this the Empress Dowager no longer intended to install Chengsi or Sansi as heir.
translations.idiomatic: From that point the Empress Dowager abandoned any plan to make Chengsi or Sansi crown prince.

sentences.zh: 孫萬榮之圍幽州也，移檄朝廷曰：「何不歸我廬陵王？」

translations.literal: When Sun Wanrong besieged You Prefecture, he sent a proclamation to the court, saying, "Why not restore to us the Prince of Luling?"
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Wanrong besieged You Prefecture, he sent a proclamation to the court asking, "Why not restore the Prince of Luling to us?"

sentences.zh: 吉頊與張易之、昌宗皆為控鶴監供奉，易之兄弟親狎之。

translations.literal: Ji Xu, Zhang Yizhi, and Zhang Changzong all served as attendants in the Crane-Control Office; the Zhang brothers were close and familiar with him.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Xu, Zhang Yizhi, and Zhang Changzong all served as attendants in the Crane-Control Office, and the Zhang brothers were on intimate terms with him.

sentences.zh: 頊從容說二人曰：「公兄弟貴寵如此，非以德業取之也，天下側目切齒多矣。

translations.literal: Xu calmly advised the two, saying, "You brothers enjoy such exalted favor—not because of virtue and achievement; many under Heaven glower and gnash their teeth.
translations.idiomatic: Xu calmly told the two brothers, "You enjoy such rank and favor, yet not because of virtue or achievement. Many under Heaven watch you with hatred and clenched teeth.

sentences.zh: 不有大功於天下，何以自全？

translations.literal: Without great merit for the realm, how can you preserve yourselves?
translations.idiomatic: Without great service to the realm, how will you save yourselves?

sentences.zh: 竊為公憂之！」

translations.literal: I privately worry for you!"
translations.idiomatic: I worry for you in private!"

sentences.zh: 二人懼，涕泣問計。

translations.literal: The two were afraid and, weeping, asked his counsel.
translations.idiomatic: The two were frightened and, weeping, asked what they should do.

sentences.zh: 頊曰：「天下士庶未忘唐德，鹹復思廬陵王。

translations.literal: Xu said, "Scholars and commoners under Heaven have not forgotten Tang virtue; all again yearn for the Prince of Luling.
translations.idiomatic: Xu said, "Gentry and commoners under Heaven have not forgotten Tang's grace. All again look to the Prince of Luling.
