translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager ordered him to sit and questioned him; Xu said, "When earth and water are mixed into mud, is there contention?"

sentences.zh: 太后曰：「無之。」

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager said, "There is not."
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager said, "There is not."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「分半為佛，半為天尊，有爭乎？」

translations.literal: He also said, "When half is made Buddha and half the Heavenly Lord, is there contention?"
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "When half is made Buddha and half the Heavenly Lord, is there contention?"

sentences.zh: 曰：「有爭矣。」

translations.literal: She said, "There is contention."
translations.idiomatic: She said, "There is contention."

sentences.zh: 頊頓首曰：「宗室、外戚各當其分，則天下安。

translations.literal: Xu bowed his head and said, "The imperial clan and the maternal kin should each keep to their proper place, then all under Heaven will be secure.
translations.idiomatic: Xu bowed his head and said, "The imperial clan and the maternal kin should each keep to their proper place, then all under Heaven will be secure.

sentences.zh: 今太子已立而外戚猶為王，此陛下驅之使他日必爭，兩不得安也。」

translations.literal: The crown prince has already been established, yet the maternal kin still hold princely rank—this is Your Majesty driving them so that they must contend someday; neither side can be secure."
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince has already been established, yet the maternal kin still hold princely rank—this is Your Majesty driving them so that they must contend someday; neither side can be secure."

sentences.zh: 太后曰：「朕亦知之。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager said, "I know this too.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager said, "I know this too.

sentences.zh: 然業已如是，不可何如。」

translations.literal: Yet matters have already come to this; nothing can be done."
translations.idiomatic: Yet matters have already come to this; nothing can be done."

sentences.zh: 臘月，辛巳，立故太孫重潤為邵王，其弟重茂為北海王。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on xinsi, the former Grand Heir Chongrun was enfeoffed as Prince of Shao, and his younger brother Chongmao as Prince of Beihai.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on xinsi, the former Grand Heir Chongrun was enfeoffed as Prince of Shao, and his younger brother Chongmao as Prince of Beihai.

sentences.zh: 太后問鸞台侍郎、同平章事陸元方以外事，對曰：「臣備位宰相，有大事不敢不以聞；

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager asked Luantai Vice Minister and Associate Counselor Lu Yuanfang about outside affairs; he replied, "Your subject holds the post of chancellor; on great matters I dare not fail to report them;
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager asked Luantai Vice Minister and Associate Counselor Lu Yuanfang about outside affairs; he replied, "Your subject holds the post of chancellor; on great matters I dare not fail to report them;

sentences.zh: 人間細事，不足煩聖聽。」

translations.literal: petty affairs among the people are not worth troubling Your Majesty's ears."
translations.idiomatic: petty affairs among the people are not worth troubling Your Majesty's ears."

sentences.zh: 由是忤旨。

translations.literal: Thereby he offended her intent.
translations.idiomatic: Thereby he offended her intent.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，罷為司禮卿。

translations.literal: On gengyin, he was removed and made Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin, he was removed and made Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 元方為人清謹，再為宰相，太后每有遷除，多訪之，元方密封以進，未嘗漏露。

translations.literal: Yuanfang was by nature pure and careful; twice serving as chancellor, whenever the Empress Dowager had appointments and removals she often consulted him; Yuanfang sealed his recommendations and submitted them, never leaking them.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanfang was by nature pure and careful; twice serving as chancellor, whenever the Empress Dowager had appointments and removals she often consulted him; Yuanfang sealed his recommendations and submitted them, never leaking them.

sentences.zh: 臨終，悉取奏稿焚之，曰：「吾於人多陰德，子孫其未衰乎！」

translations.literal: At his death he took all his memorial drafts and burned them, saying, "I have done much hidden good for many people; may my descendants not yet decline!"
translations.idiomatic: At his death he took all his memorial drafts and burned them, saying, "I have done much hidden good for many people; may my descendants not yet decline!"

sentences.zh: 以西突厥竭忠事主可汗斛瑟羅為平西軍大總管，鎮碎葉。

translations.literal: Husi Luo, qaghan of the Western Turks who exhaustively served his lord with loyalty, was made Grand Commander of the Pacified West Army and stationed at Suiye.
translations.idiomatic: Husi Luo, qaghan of the Western Turks who exhaustively served his lord with loyalty, was made Grand Commander of the Pacified West Army and stationed at Suiye.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，以狄仁傑為內史。

translations.literal: On dingyou, Di Renjie was made Internal Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou, Di Renjie was made Internal Secretary.

sentences.zh: 庚子，以文昌左丞書巨源為納言。

translations.literal: On gengzi, Left Vice Director of the Literary Flourishing Bureau Shu Juyuan was made Counselor of State.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi, Left Vice Director of the Literary Flourishing Bureau Shu Juyuan was made Counselor of State.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，太后幸嵩山；

translations.literal: On yisi, the Empress Dowager visited Mount Song;
translations.idiomatic: On yisi, the Empress Dowager visited Mount Song;

sentences.zh: 春，一月，丁卯，幸汝州之溫湯；

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on dingmao, she visited the hot springs of Ruzhou;
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on dingmao, she visited the hot springs of Ruzhou;

sentences.zh: 戊寅，還神都。

translations.literal: On wuyin, she returned to the Divine Capital.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin, she returned to the Divine Capital.

sentences.zh: 作三陽宮於告成之石淙。

translations.literal: The Three Yangs Palace was built at Shicong in Gaocheng.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Yangs Palace was built at Shicong in Gaocheng.

sentences.zh: 二月，乙未，同鳳閣鸞台三品豆盧欽望罷為太子賓客。

translations.literal: In the second month, on yiwei, Counselor of Third Rank at Fengge and Luantai Doulu Qinwang was removed and made Guest of the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on yiwei, Counselor of Third Rank at Fengge and Luantai Doulu Qinwang was removed and made Guest of the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 三月，以吐谷渾青海王宣超為烏地也拔勤忠可汗。

translations.literal: In the third month, Xuan Chao, King of Qinghai of the Tuyuhun, was made Qaghan of Wudiye Baleqinzhong.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, Xuan Chao, King of Qinghai of the Tuyuhun, was made Qaghan of Wudiye Baleqinzhong.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，戊申，太后幸三陽宮避暑，有胡僧邀車駕觀葬捨利，太后許之。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on wushen, the Empress Dowager visited the Three Yangs Palace to escape the heat; a barbarian monk invited the imperial carriage to view the burial of relics, and the Empress Dowager consented.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on wushen, the Empress Dowager visited the Three Yangs Palace to escape the heat; a barbarian monk invited the imperial carriage to view the burial of relics, and the Empress Dowager consented.

sentences.zh: 狄仁傑跪於馬前曰：「佛者戎狄之神，不足以屈天下之主。

translations.literal: Di Renjie knelt before the horse and said, "The Buddha is the god of the barbarians and is not fit to make the lord of all under Heaven bow.
translations.idiomatic: Di Renjie knelt before the horse and said, "The Buddha is the god of the barbarians and is not fit to make the lord of all under Heaven bow.

sentences.zh: 彼胡僧詭譎，直欲邀致萬乘，以惑遠近之人耳。

translations.literal: That barbarian monk is deceitful and cunning; he simply wishes to lure the Son of Heaven to delude people near and far.
translations.idiomatic: That barbarian monk is deceitful and cunning; he simply wishes to lure the Son of Heaven to delude people near and far.

sentences.zh: 山路險狹，不容侍衛，非萬乘所宜臨也。」

translations.literal: The mountain road is narrow and perilous and cannot accommodate guards; it is not fitting for the Son of Heaven to go there."
translations.idiomatic: The mountain road is narrow and perilous and cannot accommodate guards; it is not fitting for the Son of Heaven to go there."

sentences.zh: 太后中道而還，曰：「以成吾直臣之氣。」

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager turned back midway and said, "Thus to complete the mettle of my upright minister."
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager turned back midway and said, "Thus to give full scope to the mettle of my upright minister."

sentences.zh: 五月，己酉朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on jiyou, the first day of the new moon, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on jiyou, the new moon, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 太后使洪州僧胡超合長生藥，三年而成，所費巨萬。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager had the Hongzhou monk Hu Chao compound an elixir of long life; after three years it was finished, at a cost of tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager had the Hongzhou monk Hu Chao compound an elixir of long life; after three years it was finished, at a cost of tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 太后服之，疾小瘳。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager took it and her illness eased somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager took it, and her illness eased somewhat.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，赦天下，改元久視；

translations.literal: On guichou, a general amnesty was proclaimed and the era name was changed to Jiushi;
translations.idiomatic: On guichou, the court proclaimed a general amnesty and changed the era name to Jiushi;

sentences.zh: 去天冊金輪大聖之號。

translations.literal: the titles Tianche, Jinlun, and Dasheng were removed.
translations.idiomatic: the titles Tianche, Jinlun, and Dasheng were dropped.

sentences.zh: 六月，改控鶴為奉宸府，以張易之為奉宸令。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, the Crane-Control Office was renamed the Palace Attendance Bureau, and Zhang Yizhi was made its director.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, the Crane-Control Office was renamed the Palace Attendance Bureau, and Zhang Yizhi was made its director.

sentences.zh: 太后每內殿曲宴，輒引諸武、易之及弟秘書監昌宗飲博嘲謔。

translations.literal: Whenever the Empress Dowager held informal banquets in the inner palace, she would summon the Wu princes, Yizhi, and his younger brother Secretariat Director Changzong to drink, gamble, and jest.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the Empress Dowager held informal banquets in the inner palace, she would summon the Wu princes, Yizhi, and his younger brother Secretariat Director Changzong to drink, gamble, and jest.

sentences.zh: 太后欲掩其跡，乃命易之、昌宗與文學之士李嶠等修《三教珠英》於內殿。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager wished to conceal these affairs and therefore ordered Yizhi, Changzong, and the literary scholar Li Qiao and others to compile "Pearls of the Three Teachings" in the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager wished to conceal these affairs and therefore ordered Yizhi, Changzong, and the literary scholar Li Qiao and others to compile "Pearls of the Three Teachings" in the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 武三思奏昌宗乃王子晉後身。

translations.literal: Wu Sansi memorialized that Changzong was the reincarnation of Prince Zijin.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sansi memorialized that Changzong was the reincarnation of Prince Zijin.

sentences.zh: 太后命昌宗衣羽衣，吹笙，乘木鶴於庭中；

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager had Changzong dress in feather robes, play the sheng, and ride a wooden crane in the courtyard;
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager had Changzong dress in feather robes, play the sheng, and ride a wooden crane in the courtyard;

sentences.zh: 文士皆賦詩以美之。

translations.literal: the literary gentlemen all composed poems to praise him.
translations.idiomatic: the literary gentlemen all composed poems in praise of him.

sentences.zh: 太后又多選美少年為奉宸內供奉，右補闕朱敬則諫曰：「陛下內寵有易之、昌宗，足矣。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager also selected many handsome youths as inner attendants of the Palace Attendance Bureau; Right Remonstrator Zhu Jingze remonstrated, saying, "Your Majesty's inner favorites in Yizhi and Changzong are enough.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager also selected many handsome youths as inner attendants of the Palace Attendance Bureau; Right Remonstrator Zhu Jingze remonstrated, saying, "Your Majesty already has Yizhi and Changzong as inner favorites—that is enough.

sentences.zh: 近聞左監門衛長史侯祥等，明自媒衒，丑慢不恥，求為奉宸內供奉，無禮無儀，溢於朝聽。

translations.literal: Recently I have heard that Left Gate Guard Chief Clerk Hou Xiang and others openly peddle themselves, shameless in ugliness and insolence, seeking appointment as inner attendants of the Palace Attendance Bureau—without ritual or decorum, overflowing into the court's hearing.
translations.idiomatic: Recently I have heard that Left Gate Guard Chief Clerk Hou Xiang and others openly peddle themselves, shameless in their vulgarity and insolence, seeking appointment as inner attendants of the Palace Attendance Bureau—without ritual or decorum, to the scandal of the whole court.

sentences.zh: 臣職在諫諍，不敢不奏。」

translations.literal: Your servant's duty is remonstrance; I dare not fail to report this."
translations.idiomatic: Your servant's duty is remonstrance; I dare not fail to report this."

sentences.zh: 太后勞之曰：「非卿直言，朕不知此。」

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager thanked him, saying, "Had you not spoken plainly, We would not have known this."
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager thanked him, saying, "Had you not spoken plainly, I would not have known this."

sentences.zh: 賜彩百段。

translations.literal: She granted him one hundred lengths of colored silk.
translations.idiomatic: She granted him one hundred lengths of colored silk.

sentences.zh: 易之、昌宗競以豪侈相勝。

translations.literal: Yizhi and Changzong vied with each other in extravagance.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhi and Changzong vied with each other in extravagance.

sentences.zh: 弟昌儀為洛陽令，請屬無不從。

translations.literal: Their younger brother Changyi was prefect of Luoyang; no request he made on another's behalf was refused.
translations.idiomatic: Their younger brother Changyi was prefect of Luoyang; no request he made on another's behalf was refused.

sentences.zh: 嘗早朝，有選人姓薛，以金五十兩並狀邀其馬而賂之。

translations.literal: Once at the early audience, a candidate surnamed Xue offered fifty liang of gold together with his petition, intercepting Changyi's horse to bribe him.
translations.idiomatic: Once at the early audience, a candidate surnamed Xue offered fifty liang of gold together with his petition, intercepting Changyi's horse to bribe him.

sentences.zh: 昌儀受金，至朝堂，以狀授天官侍郎張錫。

translations.literal: Changyi accepted the gold and, upon reaching the court hall, handed the petition to Celestial Offices Vice Minister Zhang Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Changyi accepted the gold and, upon reaching the court hall, handed the petition to Celestial Offices Vice Minister Zhang Xi.

sentences.zh: 數日，錫失其狀，以問昌儀，昌儀罵曰：「不了事人！

translations.literal: Several days later Xi lost the petition and asked Changyi about it; Changyi cursed him, saying, "Useless man!
translations.idiomatic: Several days later Xi lost the petition and asked Changyi about it; Changyi cursed him, saying, "Useless man!

sentences.zh: 我亦不記，但姓薛者即與之。」

translations.literal: I do not remember either—just give the appointment to whoever is surnamed Xue."
translations.idiomatic: I do not remember either—just give the appointment to whoever is surnamed Xue."

sentences.zh: 錫懼，退，索在銓姓薛者六十餘人，悉留注官。

translations.literal: Xi was afraid; he withdrew and searched out more than sixty men surnamed Xue on the rolls, and registered appointments for them all.
translations.idiomatic: Xi was afraid; he withdrew and found more than sixty men surnamed Xue on the rolls, and registered appointments for them all.

sentences.zh: 錫，文瓘之兄之子也。

translations.literal: Xi was the son of Wenjin's elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: Xi was a nephew of Zhang Wenjin.

sentences.zh: 初，契丹將李楷固，善用絲□索及騎射、舞槊，每陷陳，如鶻入烏群，所向披靡。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Khitan general Li Kaigu was skilled with silk [□] ropes, mounted archery, and spear-dancing; whenever he charged the formation it was like a hawk entering a flock of crows—wherever he turned, none could stand before him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the Khitan general Li Kaigu was skilled with silk ropes, mounted archery, and spear-dancing; whenever he charged the formation it was like a hawk diving into a flock of crows—wherever he turned, none could stand before him.

sentences.zh: 黃獐之戰，張玄遇、麻仁節皆為所絲□。

translations.literal: At the battle of Huangzhang, Zhang Xuanyu and Ma Renjie were both caught by his ropes [□].
translations.idiomatic: At the battle of Huangzhang, Zhang Xuanyu and Ma Renjie were both caught by his ropes.

sentences.zh: 又有駱務整者，亦為契丹將，屢敗唐兵。

translations.literal: There was also Luo Wuzheng, likewise a Khitan general, who repeatedly defeated Tang forces.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Luo Wuzheng, likewise a Khitan general, who repeatedly defeated Tang forces.

sentences.zh: 及孫萬榮死，二人來降。

translations.literal: When Sun Wanrong died, the two came to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Wanrong died, the two came to surrender.

sentences.zh: 有司責其後至，奏請族之。

translations.literal: The responsible offices blamed them for arriving late and memorialized that their clans be executed to the last.
translations.idiomatic: The responsible offices blamed them for arriving late and memorialized that their clans be executed to the last.

sentences.zh: 狄仁傑曰：「楷固等並驍勇絕倫，能盡力於所事，必能盡力於我。

translations.literal: Di Renjie said, "Kaigu and the others are all peerless in valor; they gave their full strength to those they served and will surely give their full strength to us.
translations.idiomatic: Di Renjie said, "Kaigu and the others are peerless in valor; they gave their full strength to those they served and will surely give their full strength to us.

sentences.zh: 若撫之以德，皆為我用矣。」

translations.literal: If we treat them with virtue, all will serve our use."
translations.idiomatic: If we treat them with kindness, all will serve our use."

sentences.zh: 奏請赦之。

translations.literal: He memorialized asking that they be pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized asking that they be pardoned.

sentences.zh: 所親皆止之，仁傑曰：「苟利於國，豈為身謀！」

translations.literal: Those close to him all tried to stop him; Renjie said, "If it benefits the state, how can I scheme for myself!"
translations.idiomatic: Those close to him all tried to stop him; Renjie said, "If it benefits the state, how can I scheme for myself!"

sentences.zh: 太后用其言，赦之。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager followed his advice and pardoned them.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager followed his advice and pardoned them.

sentences.zh: 又請與之官，太后以楷固為左玉鈐衛將軍，務整為右武威衛將軍，使將兵擊契丹餘黨，悉平之。」」

translations.literal: He also asked that they be given offices; the Empress Dowager appointed Kaigu Left Jade Tally Guard General and Wuzheng Right Martial Might Guard General, and had them lead troops to strike the remaining Khitan partisans, pacifying them all.”
translations.idiomatic: He also asked that they be given offices; the Empress Dowager appointed Kaigu Left Jade Tally Guard General and Wuzheng Right Martial Might Guard General, and had them lead troops against the remaining Khitan partisans, pacifying them all.”
